svg.title: One word: queue or stack
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “One word: queue or stack” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. A whiteboard sketch showing the same seven-node graph twice, once visited in breadth-first level order with dashed level rings and the word QUEUE circled, once visited in depth-first order with the word STACK circled, and the two nearly identical code fragments differing only in popleft versus pop; a topological sort peeling zero-in-degree nodes off a five-node directed graph with in-degrees written under each; the same graph with one red back edge added leaving three nodes whose in-degree never reaches zero, ringed in red as the cycle; and a memory comparison of 52.3 megabytes for an adjacency list against 1,250 megabytes for a bitset adjacency matrix.
svg.text: draw it from memory, then compare
